AbstractText.Label: PURPOSE
AbstractText.content: To evaluate low versus high dose plaque brachytherapy for juxtapapillary choroidal melanoma.

AbstractText.Label: INTERVENTION
AbstractText.content: Iodine-125 plaque brachytherapy. Eyes were divided into apex low dose (LD) and high dose (HD) groups (< or > median apex dose 84.35 Gy). Main outcome measures were time to distant failure, local failure, death, enucleation, radiation retinopathy, optic neuropathy, and best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA).

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Freedom from distant failure rates were 96% and 95% in apex LD and HD groups at five years and 77% and 95% at ten years, respectively (p = 0.84). Freedom from local failure rates were 90% in the apex LD group versus 89% in the HD group at five and ten years (p = 0.96). Apex LD and HD groups did not differ for time to death or enucleation. Five- and ten-year freedom from radiation retinopathy and optic neuropathy rates were higher in the apex LD than HD group. Loss of >3 BCVA lines, final BCVA 20/40 or better, and final BCVA 20/200 or worse were more favorable in the 5 mm LD compared to HD group. Visual acuity outcomes did not differ between apex LD and HD groups.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Low dose Iodine-125 plaque brachytherapy (67.5 - 81 Gy at tumor apex) provides safe and effective tumor control for juxtapapillary choroidal melanoma and may be associated with reduced radiation toxicity. Larger trials are needed to determine the optimal therapeutic dose for juxtapapillary choroidal melanoma.
